title: Contract output and file hygiene
explanation: The contract rules that are fact-shaped outside the task chain: one verification line, generated output not edited, workspace-relative paths, rules.lock untouched, and files placed in the declared structure.

cases.original: A single `VERIFICATION:` line is always permitted output, regardless of the requested format
cases.note: The count condition enforces "single": two or more verification facts are a violation. The round-trip's older rule still permits the line without the count; this candidate adds the limit.
cases.suggestion: Say "at most one VERIFICATION line", so the count is explicit.

cases.original: Generated output is produced by the script or workflow step that owns it, never edited in place.
cases.note: The extractor reports whether a generated file differs from what its script produced; the rule refuses a hand edit.
cases.suggestion: Say "a generated file's content comes from its generator and is never edited in place".

cases.original: Committed tool configuration uses workspace-relative paths; never an absolute home path.
cases.note: The extractor flags an absolute home path; the rule refuses it.
cases.suggestion: Keep "workspace-relative", and name the variable form (for example "the workspace folder").

cases.original: Exception: `rules.lock` is never edited by hand, by a task or a workflow step; only `tools/rules-vendor.sh` writes it.
cases.note: The rule is narrow: the path and the hand-edit fact. The vendor script is the only writer.
cases.suggestion: Keep the exception; the path is a fact, so it compiles cleanly.

cases.original: Place every new file in a directory listed here or in the permitted root set.
cases.note: The extractor reports whether a new path belongs to the declared structure; whether the chosen directory is the right one is a review.
cases.suggestion: Say "a new file's directory is in the declared structure".
